oewn-02752958-n.learner: a single thing made of parts that have been fitted together
examples: The display stand was a wooden assembly of shelves and panels.

oewn-02752795-n.learner: a set of machine parts that fit together to make one unit that works on its own
examples: The mechanic replaced the whole brake assembly.

oewn-00913832-n.learner: the act of building something, such as a machine
examples: Assembly of the engine took two days.

oewn-02605525-v.learner: to not be able to do something
examples: I fail to see why you are so angry.
The brakes failed halfway down the hill.

oewn-02527985-v.learner: to not do as much as is expected of you
examples: He failed in his duty to protect them.

oewn-00561324-v.learner: to turn out to be not enough
examples: By the end of the winter the food supply had failed.

oewn-02529187-v.learner: to not get a good enough mark to pass a test or a course
examples: She failed her driving test twice.
His eyesight began to fail as he grew old.

oewn-02529450-v.learner: to decide that someone or something is not acceptable
examples: The examiner failed him for driving too fast.

oewn-02323383-v.learner: to be unable to pay debts, or to run out of money and close down
examples: Many small banks failed during the crisis.

oewn-00416239-n.learner: the usual way that a person or group does things
examples: It was his fashion to rise early and walk before breakfast.

oewn-10103127-n.learner: an informal word used when speaking directly to a man
examples: Say, fellow, you dropped your hat!

oewn-13765240-n.learner: either one of a pair of things
examples: One glove was on the table, but its fellow was never found.

oewn-11712326-n.learner: in the study of plants, either of the two parts into which a flower's ring of petals, or the green cup around it, is split
examples: The lower lip of the flower gives bees a place to land.

oewn-01944179-n.learner: either the outer edge or the inner edge of the opening of the shell of a snail or a related animal
examples: The outer lip of the shell was thick and smooth.

oewn-00778568-v.learner: to get someone to do something by being charming
examples: With her warm smile she tempted the shy boy to join the dance.

oewn-01811737-v.learner: to try to lead someone into sex or into doing something wrong
examples: The serpent tempted Eve in the garden.

connotation.why: frames the attraction as leading toward wrongdoing

oewn-00786231-v.learner: to test something too boldly, as if nothing could go wrong
examples: Climbing without a rope is tempting fate.

connotation.why: casts the risk-taking as overconfident presumption

oewn-00419407-n.learner: the act of bothering or annoying someone
examples: The children's endless vexation of their teacher wore her out.
The youth of the town gathered in the square.

oewn-04935762-n.learner: the fresh, lively quality that a young person has
examples: At sixty he still had the youth and energy of a boy.

oewn-15290845-n.learner: an early stage in the growth of something
examples: In the youth of the railway, trains were slow and uncomfortable.

oewn-09844011-n.learner: the people who are in charge and control others, usually called the authorities
examples: The authorities closed the road after the flood.

oewn-08354251-n.learner: a government body set up to run some part of public business
examples: The local water authority raised its prices.

oewn-05705328-n.learner: the feeling of being sure, and of believing in yourself and what you can do
examples: She played the piano with such authority that no one doubted her.

oewn-06423235-n.learner: a book or other piece of writing that people trust as the final word on a subject
examples: This dictionary is the standard authority on English spelling.

oewn-09950876-n.learner: a person who teaches someone privately, for example in singing or acting
examples: She hired a voice coach before the audition.

oewn-03901563-n.learner: a railway car that passengers ride in
examples: We found two empty seats in the last coach of the train.
